label: Motacilla_aguimp
summary: The African pied wagtail, or African wagtail, (Motacilla aguimp) is a species of bird in the family Motacillidae.

appearance.description: A striking black and white wagtail with black upperparts contrasting with white underparts, it has a white supercilium and a white patch in the folded wing. Juvenile birds are greyer, while birds of the nominate subspecies show grey flanks. They are 20 cm (7.9 in) long.
appearance.colors: A striking black and white wagtail with black upperparts contrasting with white underparts, it has a white supercilium and a white patch in the folded wing.
appearance.wings: A striking black and white wagtail with black upperparts contrasting with white underparts, it has a white supercilium and a white patch in the folded wing.

juvenile.notes: Juvenile birds are greyer, while birds of the nominate subspecies show grey flanks.

where_found.habitat: The African pied wagtail is found in sub-Saharan Africa from the Eastern Cape north to extreme southern Egypt and from Guinea to western Eritrea and Somalia. It is a vagrant to Burkina Faso, Gambia, Mauritania,Uganda and the Western Cape.
